Exercise 2.36(a)-(d): the involution subposet Invol(W) is graded with rank r(w) = (l(w) + a-l(w))/2, has Mobius function (-1)^{r(w)-r(u)}, and is shellable in types A, B and D

sources.title: R. W. Carter, Conjugacy classes in the Weyl group, Compositio Mathematica 25 (1972) 1-59 (Numdam full text, 60 PDF pages)
sources.locator: Introduction and section 2 'Products of reflections', printed pp. 1-5: the root-system setup, Lemmas 1-5 with the proofs of Lemmas 2, 3 and 4. Section 3 and later (admissible diagrams and the conjugacy classification) were not read for this batch.

contents.name: Section 2 setup: a finite W-stable set Phi of nonzero vectors satisfying the root-system axioms (i)-(iv), and W generated by the reflections w_r
contents.reason: Carter's integrality and irreducibility axioms are crystallographic and fail for the finite Coxeter types H3, H4 and I2(5) covered by this page; the page consumes the run's Coxeter-form reflection suppliers instead of these axioms.

contents.name: Lemma 1: an element of W fixing all vectors of a set S pointwise is a product of reflections each fixing S pointwise
Lemma 2 with proof: l(w) equals the number of eigenvalues of w on V different from 1
Lemma 2 applied in type A: reflection length of a permutation is n minus its number of cycles
Lemma 3 with proof: the product w_{r_1}...w_{r_k} is reduced if and only if r_1,...,r_k are linearly independent
Lemma 4: if -1 lies in W then Phi contains l mutually orthogonal roots
contents.reason: The orthogonal-root structure of the element -1 is not used by the reflection-length, absolute-order or moved-space claims of this page, and no planned page of this run consumes it.

contents.name: Lemma 5: every involution of W is a product of l(w) commuting reflections
contents.reason: Involutions and their commuting reflection factorizations are not consumed by this page's order-theoretic and moved-space claims.

sources.title: T. Brady and C. Watt, Lattices in finite real reflection groups (arXiv:math/0501502, 29 PDF pages)
sources.locator: Introduction and section 2, printed pp. 1-3 (reflection length, absolute order, moved and fixed spaces, the main result of [7] and notes (1)-(7)); the opening of section 3 through Note 3.5, printed pp. 3-6; and the opening paragraphs of section 4, printed pp. 8-9, with the A3 intersection example. Sections 5-8 were not read for this batch.

contents.name: Section 2: reflection length l(v) as the least k with v a product of k reflections, and the absolute order u <= w iff l(w)=l(u)+l(u^{-1}w), with the reading 'a shortest factorization of u is a prefix of one of w'
Section 2: the moved space M(A) = im(A-I) and the fixed space F(A) = ker(A-I), with F(A) = F(A^{-1})
Section 2: M(A) = F(A)^perp
Section 2: the main result of [7] - if V is a subspace of M(A) then there is a unique B in O(n) with M(B) = V and B <= A
Section 2 note (1): if alpha <= beta then M(alpha) is contained in M(beta) and F(beta) is contained in F(alpha)
Section 2 note (2): v in M(alpha) implies R(v) alpha = alpha R[alpha^{-1}(v)]
contents.reason: The conjugation identity used on this page is the in-run root-reflection dictionary rho(w s w^{-1}) = r_{rho(w)e_s}; this note's operator identity is not consumed by the selected proof route.

contents.name: Section 2 notes (3) and (6): interval translation under u -> alpha^{-1}u and under right multiplication
contents.reason: Invariance of intervals under left and right multiplication by fixed elements is not used by the reflection-length, rigidity or worked-example claims of this page.

contents.name: Section 2 note (4): if alpha, beta <= delta and M(alpha) is contained in M(beta) then alpha <= beta
Section 2 note (5): for a reduced factorization alpha = R_1...R_k one has M(R_j) in M(R_1 alpha) for j >= 2
contents.reason: The suffix-inclusion property of reduced factorizations is not used; the independence statement of this page is proved from the telescoping identity of a factorization instead.

contents.name: Section 2 note (7): R_1R_2 <= alpha iff R_2 <= R_1 alpha iff R_1 <= alpha R_2
contents.reason: The rank-two reflection-shifting equivalence is not part of this page's claims and has no consumer among its items or planned consumers.

contents.name: Section 2 closing: facts about spherical simplices determined by linearly independent sets of positive roots
contents.reason: Spherical simplices are not consumed by this page; its spherical and chamber geometry comes from the finite reflection arrangement page of this run.
